# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

I'm the last to act this round, and I've just received a gesture from Blind (who acted before me). Since Blind cannot see, they wouldn't gesture unless it means something pre-agreed — but this is turn 1, nothing is established yet. This is likely just Blind signaling "I'm here, waiting for info" or testing the channel.

I need to start giving Blind (via Mute, since I can't speak to Blind directly in a way Mute doesn't relay... wait, actually checking channels: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So I CAN speak directly to Blind.

I should report what I see plainly and clearly, since Mute needs this cross-referenced with the manual, and Blind needs actionable info once we know what to do. I'll describe the whole board factually first.

```
speak(text="Deaf report: Display shows 9. Light is red. Strip has three segments painted green, yellow, yellow in that order. Keypad is engraved with 1 equals 1, 2 equals 5, 3 equals 2, 4 equals 8, and it has a 1 digit entry slot, currently empty. Six wires numbered 1 to 6, colors in order: yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏]

Mute sent me 14 gesture symbols (☝ repeated with ✋ breaks) - this looks like it could be encoding numbers via tally marks, using ✋ as a separator. Let me count: ☝☝☝☝☝ (5) ✋ ☝☝☝ (3) ✋ ☝☝☝☝ (4). That could be "5, 3, 4" — but I don't know what that maps to yet. Since Mute can't speak and I can't hear anyway, gestures are our only channel, and Mute is being creative since I can see gestures.

The display changed from 9 to 3, light changed from red to yellow. Everything else is static. This suggests DISPLAY and LIGHT are dynamic/changing each turn, while STRIP, KEYPAD, WIRES are fixed properties of the bomb.

Blind sent 🙏 which I can't interpret meaningfully yet without more shared context - possibly "please" or acknowledging receipt.

I should keep reporting the current state plainly, and try to acknowledge Mute's count in case it's meaningful, while flagging the changes I noticed.

```
speak(text="Deaf report: Display now shows 3, changed from 9. Light now yellow, changed from red. Strip, keypad, and wires all unchanged from before: strip green yellow yellow, keypad 1 equals 1, 2 equals 5, 3 equals 2, 4 equals 8 with 1 digit entry empty, wires yellow white blue red purple green in slots 1 through 6.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤙]

Mute repeated the exact same gesture sequence: 5, 3, 4 (using ✋ as separator, ☝ as tally). This is consistent across two turns, so it's likely a fixed instruction from the manual, not something reacting to display/light changes. Since it's static, it probably references the keypad or wires — something also static. Given the keypad maps 1→1, 2→5, 3→2, 4→8, position 3 gives value 2, but "5,3,4" doesn't obviously match.

Wait — maybe it's not counts but three separate numbers: 5, 3, 4. Could be wire positions to cut, or a code sequence. Since Blind holds the manual conceptually? No — Mute holds the manual. Mute is likely relaying manual instructions to me since I can see gestures, expecting me to relay to Blind somehow — but I can also speak directly to Blind.

Display and Light keep changing each turn (9→3→2, red→yellow→red) — these might be irrelevant noise, or a countdown/state that determines timing rather than the action itself.

Blind's gesture changed to 👉🤙 — different from before, suggesting Blind is also trying to communicate something, but I can't decode arbitrary gestures without established meaning either.

I'll relay Mute's fixed sequence to Blind as numbers, and continue reporting board state, since that's my only real contribution — accurate transcription.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has signaled the same three numbers twice now: 5, 3, 4. Deaf report: Display shows 2, light is red. Strip, keypad, and wires unchanged: strip green yellow yellow, keypad 1 equals 1, 2 equals 5, 3 equals 2, 4 equals 8, one digit entry empty, wires yellow white blue red purple green.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

Mute added a trailing ✋ this time: 5, 3, 4, and then a separator with nothing after — possibly signaling "end of sequence" or that this is the complete/final instruction now that the light is green (maybe green means "go" or "safe to act"). The light has cycled red→yellow→red→green. Green could be the trigger to act.

Blind sent 🤝 - possibly "agreed" or "ready," suggesting Blind may have also received something from Mute (since Mute's gesture reaches only me, not Blind — Mute can't touch, speak only reaches those who hear, and Blind can't hear or see, so Blind gets nothing from Mute directly except gestures which Blind can't see either). So Blind is isolated from Mute entirely — Blind only receives info through me.

This means I'm the sole relay between Mute and Blind. I need to pass Mute's numbers to Blind as an instruction, and the trailing separator suggests the sequence is complete: 5, 3, 4.

Given the keypad has a 1-digit entry, "5, 3, 4" as a single digit doesn't fit directly — unless these are wire numbers (wires 1-6 exist) or steps of a sequence to perform in order (e.g., "check wire 5, wire 3, wire 4" or "cut wire 5, then 3, then 4").

I'll relay clearly to Blind and note the light is now green plus the completed sequence.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is now green, display shows 3. Mute's signal is complete now, three numbers in order: 5, then 3, then 4. Strip, keypad, wires all still unchanged from before.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[CUT] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 5 has been cut — that matches the "5" from Mute's sequence "5, 3, 4"! And the system confirms "correct wire cut" — so Blind acted on my relay and it worked. Mute's gesture is now 👍 (thumbs up), confirming this was correct.

The sequence must mean: cut wire 5, then wire 3, then wire 4, in that order. Next step should be wire 3.

Light changed to blue (new color, first time seen), display shows 5. These seem to just be cosmetic/changing indicators, not part of the actual solution, since the wire-cutting sequence directly matches Mute's numbers.

I should confirm progress to Blind and remind them of the remaining steps.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed correct: wire 5 was the right cut, Mute gave a thumbs up. Next in the sequence is wire 3, then wire 4. Current board: display 5, light blue, wire 5 now shows CUT, others unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 6 green.")
wait()
```
